data.title: Monarch Casino & Resort 3Q 2026: Revenue $146.27M, Net income $32.01M, EPS $1.76— 10-Q Summary
data.description:
Monarch Casino & Resort reported third-quarter 2026 net revenue of $146.27 million, up 2.4% from the prior-year quarter. Net income increased 1.4% to $32.01 million, while diluted EPS rose 4.1% to $1.76.

Financial Highlights

MetricCurrent quarterPrior year quarterYoY change
Revenue¹$146.27M$142.81M2.4%
Net income²$32.01M$31.58M1.4%
Diluted EPS³$1.76$1.694.1%

¹ Reported as “Net revenues”. ² Reported as “Net income”. ³ Reported as “Diluted earnings per share of common stock”.

Business Highlights

  • Casino revenue increased 3.4% in the quarter, supported by higher visitation and gaming volume.
  • For the first nine months, revenue grew 5.0%, including increases of 4.9% in casino revenue and 8.4% in hotel revenue.
  • Food and beverage revenue rose 1.3% as a 3.0% increase in revenue per cover offset a 1.7% decline in covers.
  • Hotel occupancy improved to 89.8% from 89.0%, while average daily rate and revenue per available room also edged higher.
  • Management cited strong regional economies and product quality as growth opportunities, while noting competitive and labor-cost pressures.

data.title: Forum Energy Technologies 3Q 2026: Revenue $236.8M, EPS $0.93— 10-Q Summary
data.description:
Forum Energy Technologies reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $236.8M, up 20.7% from $196.2M a year earlier. Net income was $11.2M, compared with a $20.6M net loss in the prior-year quarter, while diluted EPS was $0.93 versus a diluted loss of $1.76.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue was $236.8M, compared with $196.2M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 20.7%.
  • Net income was $11.2M, compared with a $20.6M net loss in the prior-year quarter.
  • Diluted EPS was $0.93, compared with a diluted loss of $1.76 in the prior-year quarter.

Business Highlights

  • Drilling and Completions revenue increased 25.3%, supported by subsea projects and parts, coiled tubing, wireline cable, radiators, and drilling equipment.
  • Artificial Lift and Downhole revenue grew 13.8%, driven by sand and flow control products and midstream valves, while demand for production equipment weakened.
  • Higher volume, cost-saving initiatives, and operating leverage lifted segment results. Prior-year consolidation and product-discontinuation charges also contributed to the year-over-year improvement.
  • The company said efficiency, safety, emissions goals, and long-term energy demand support its products. Its PTR acquisition expanded the business.

Original SEC Filing: FORUM ENERGY TECHNOLOGIES, INC. [ FET ] - 10-Q - Oct. 30, 2026

data.title: Enterprise Financial Services 3Q 2026: Net interest income $174.6M, Net income $42.4M, EPS $1.14— 10-Q Summary
data.description:
Enterprise Financial Services Corp reported third-quarter 2026 net interest income of $174.6 million, up 10.3% from a year earlier, while net income fell 6.2% to $42.4 million and diluted EPS declined 4.2% to $1.14.

Financial Highlights

  • Net interest income was $174.6M, compared with $158.3M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 10.3%.
  • Net income was $42.4M, compared with $45.2M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change (6.2%).
  • Diluted EPS was $1.14, compared with $1.19 in the prior-year quarter; YoY change (4.2%).

Business Highlights

  • Nine-month net interest income increased $50.9 million year over year, supported by loan and securities growth and lower funding costs.
  • Loans rose 5% to $12.3 billion, led by commercial and investor-owned real estate lending. Deposits increased $517.6 million to $15.1 billion, including growth in property management, community association and escrow deposits to $4.2 billion.
  • The 2025 acquisition of 12 branches in Arizona and Kansas expanded operations and contributed to higher staffing and operating costs.
  • Nonperforming assets reached 1.03% of assets; management cited loan workouts and related property costs as ongoing operating pressures.

Original SEC Filing: ENTERPRISE FINANCIAL SERVICES CORP [ EFSC ] - 10-Q - Oct. 30, 2026

data.title: Dividend stocks alert: Record date Mon 2 Nov: Colgate Palmolive vs Pitti Engineering vs Route Mobile vs Tanla Platforms
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 30 -- Shares of Colgate Palmolive (India), Pitti Engineering Limited, Route Mobile Limited, and Tanla Platforms Limited will remain in focus during Monday's trading session because of their scheduled dividend record dates.

These firms have fixed Monday, November 2, as the record date to determine the eligibility of shareholders for the payout. Which means that investors must own the stock before the record date to qualify for the payout.

Colgate Palmolive, on October 22, announced a dividend payout of Rs.24 per equity share last week. The board has fixed November 2 as the record date. Colgate Palmolive share price closed 2.16% lower at Rs.1594.70 per share on BSE with an MCap of Rs.43,373.55 crore on Friday.

Pitti Engineering's board of directors approved an interim dividend of Rs.2 per equity share with a face value of Rs.5 each. The company's board of directors has fixed Monday, November 2 as the record date. The stock closed 3.58% lower at Rs.851.50 per share on BSE with an Mcap of Rs.3,206.20 crore.

Route Mobile's board of directors announced Rs.4 per equity share dividend for FY27. The board fixed Monday, November 2, as the record date. The stock closed 2.89% lower at Rs.439.50 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.2,768.99 crore on Friday.

The company's board of directors approved Rs.6 per share dividend in October. The company's board of directors has fixed Monday, November 2. Tanla Platforms stock closed 2.89% lower at Rs.439.50 per share on Friday.

Out of the four companies which will trade ex-dividend on Monday, November 2, Colgate Palmolive (India) has announced the highest payout, ie of Rs.24 per share.

data.title: White House hearing on Fed's Cook delayed to December, Hassett says
data.description:
The White House has delayed until December a planned hearing into allegations of mortgage fraud by Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, President Donald Trump's top economic advisor said, though lawyers for Cook on Friday declined to confirm that any date had been agreed.

"The president has asked a small set of his people to run a completely fair process that puts all the information on the table, and then the president will decide next steps," Kevin Hassett told Bloomberg TV on Thursday. "We in the White House, the White House counsel, has worked very closely with Governor Cook's people. I think that they've agreed to a date in December to meet together and talk these things through."

Cook's lawyer, who along with Cook herself has denied any wrongdoing and called Trump's accusations a pretense to remove her because he wants the Fed to cut rates, had previously said Cook would not be available for any hearing until after the Fed's December 8-9 policy-setting meeting. A spokeswoman for her lawyer did not confirm any new date in December.

Trump has been trying to fire Cook for more than a year.

The Supreme Court in June ruled that he cannot do so "at will" but that he may be able to if he gives her a chance to defend herself against any evidence he believes shows "cause" for removal. Trump announced a fresh investigation last month and initially set November 5 as a hearing date.

Cook this week dissented on the Fed's decision to leave rates steady instead of delivering another rate hike to curb inflation, as she would have preferred. The Fed is widely expected to raise rates again in December. Trump has long railed against the Fed for not cutting rates, and accused a "political" Fed Board, which includes Cook, for keeping Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh from doing so.

Hassett, who is on the three-person committee Trump appointed to investigate Cook and recommend if she should be fired, had called Cook "partisan" last August for not vacating her post after Trump's allegations.

On Thursday he told Bloomberg TV Thursday he feels "Chairman Warsh has done a good job of allowing, you know, normal dissent and then driving a consensus."

The White House committee looking into Cook is comprised of "people of honor who are charged with looking at the evidence and correctly characterizing it in a way that people will be able to observe and criticize if they like," he said.

data.title: CBOT soybeans end mixed, notch third straight weekly loss
data.description:
Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures ended mixed on Friday on bargain-buying and signs of export demand, with deferred months ending lower, traders said.

  • While the most-active contract was up for much of the session, it eased late in the day and marked a third straight weekly loss.

  • CBOT November soybeans (SX26) settled up 2-1/2 cents at $12.22-1/4 per bushel and most-active January soybeans (SF27) ended down 1/2 cent at $12.34-1/4.

  • Some traders this week have been liquidating November soybean futures positions ahead of Friday, which is the first notice day for deliveries against the contract.

  • CBOT December soymeal (SMZ26) ended down $4.70 at $324.60 per ton, after falling to $324.40, its lowest since August 21.

  • CBOT December soyoil (BOZ26) rose 0.26 cent to finish at 65.90 cents per pound.

  • Exporters sold 165,150 metric tons of US soybeans received in the reporting period to unknown destinations for 2026/27 delivery, the US Department of Agriculture said in its daily reporting system on Friday.

  • USDA also reported that an additional 132,000 tons of US soybeans were sold to unknown destinations for the 2026/2027 marketing year.

  • The US soybean harvest was winding down but Midwest farmers continued to bring in crops ahead of wet weather expected next week, analysts said.

data.title: AXT Stock Falls Despite 162% Revenue Jump on Indium Phosphide
data.description:
AXT , which makes indium phosphide and other compound semiconductor substrates used in data center optical connections, reported third-quarter non-GAAP EPS of $0.41, above the analysts' consensus of $0.31, on revenue of $73.4 million, ahead of the $66 million estimate. GAAP gross margin widened to 56.0% from 22.3%, and GAAP EPS was $0.39, against a loss of $0.04 a year earlier. The diluted share count rose to 65.9 million from 43.8 million, while cash grew to $485.5 million from $120.3 million at the end of 2025.

Young said AXT has more than doubled its indium phosphide capacity this year and has more than quadrupled our 2026 indium phosphide revenue opportunity through productivity gains and larger-diameter products.

data.title: ICE Closing Review: Canola Finds Traction
data.description:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba-- Intercontinental Exchange canola futures posted gains on Friday, halting a multi-session slide after getting support from comparable oils.

With the threat of renewed fighting in the Middle East, crude oil was up sharply on Friday, with the spillover flowing into

the vegetable oils. That saw canola underpinned by increases in Chicago soybeans and soyoil, as well as Malaysian palm oil and European rapeseed.

Some pressure came from losses in Chicago soymeal.

Despite today's improvement, the January canola contract remained behind most of its major moving averages, weighing on canola values.

Producer deliveries of canola slipped during the week ended Oct. 25 to 445,900 tonnes. The year-to-date of 5.43 million tonnes

was 1.32 million more than a year ago.

Canola exports nudged up on the week at 238,000 tonnes. Cumulative exports nearly topped 1.89 million tonnes, compared to 1.23 million this time last year.

Domestic use was relatively steady at 196,300 tonnes with the running total of almost 2.99 million tonnes slightly ahead of last year.

The Canadian dollar was higher on Friday afternoon, with the loonie at 71.65 U.S. cents, compared to Wednesday's close of 71.51.

There were 55,387 canola contracts traded on Friday, compared to 78,331 on Thursday. Spreading accounted for 26,094 contracts traded.

data.title: Alphabet Convertible Preferred Now Yields Over 7.5%. There's a Catch. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Andrew Bary

Alphabet's mandatory convertible preferred stock, which it issued as part of its $85 billion equity capital raising plan in June, has gotten hit along with the company's common stock and now yields more than 7.5%.

The problem for investors is that the convertible preferred securities will pay that rate only until May 2029, at which point the preferred will be converted into common shares at what could be a discount to their face value of $50 a share and their current price of around $41.

Alphabet's voting common stock (GOOGL) was off another 1.7% to $278.95 Friday after dropping 12% Thursday in the wake of its disappointing third quarter earnings report.

The company has two issues of mandatory convertible preferred outstanding.

The securities exchangeable for Alphabet's voting shares (GOOGL) are traded under ticker GOOGM and fetch $41.19, down 1.3% in the session, and the convertibles exchangeable into the nonvoting stock (GOOGN) are at $41.25, also down 1.3%. The nonvoting common is traded as GOOG.

In June, Alphabet issued a total of $16.6 billion of the 6.25% mandatory convertible preferred shares divided equally into the two parts. There were 167.5 million shares in each offering priced at $50 a share. At the time, Alphabet's common stock was trading around $355 a share.

Mandatory convertible preferred shares, as the name implied, will automatically get exchanged for common stock. In the case of the Alphabet deals, that's due to occur in May 2029.

The structure is such that investors don't get the downside protection common in traditional convertible bonds and preferred. With a traditional convertible bond, the holder gets paid back the original offering price at maturity and participates in any gains in the issuer's underlying common stock.

Issuers like mandatory convertibles — or "mandies" — because of this feature. They'd rather not provide downside protection. And the securities have been very popular this year with Meta Platforms recently selling a large, $12.5 billion deal. But the structure works against investors in a down market. Mandatory convertibles amount to high-yield versions of the issuer's common stock rather than a traditional convertible.

With the Alphabet offerings, investors in the convertible are due to get roughly 0.14 common shares for each convertible preferred share based on current prices. That value is now about $39 per convertible preferred share, Barron's calculates.

So the holder of the preferred shares will get a nice yield of 7.6% until May 2029, but that income will be offset by a decline in the value of the preferred shares assuming no change in Alphabet common. The preferred does offer a much higher yield than the common now yielding just 0.3%.

Since the offering was made, the convertible preferred has outperformed the common stock, falling about 18% against a 21% drop in the stock. So investors have been better off in the convertible preferred.

That's some comfort in a tough period for Alphabet stock.

Write to Andrew Bary at andrew.bary@barrons.com
